purpose: Teach: 惣菜/祇園/ビリヤード/ツバメ/炭水化物/クールビズ/高島屋/芸者

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お母様は惣菜屋を営まれたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when I was young, your mother ran a prepared food shop.
lines.style: Soft, settled voice. Gentle hand on a memory. Slow pace, like he's reaching back across years. Warmth without urgency.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、祇園で芸妓のお話を聞かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mmm, and you heard all those stories about the geishas in Gion, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Bright remembering, like she's pleased to hold this piece of him. Voice carries affection wrapped around a question. Conversational rhythm, gently playful.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとビリヤード場で遊んだぞ
lines.en: And when I was young, your father and I used to play pool together.
lines.style: Same wistful reach, but with a thread of quiet joy. Slight rise on 「遊んだ」 — the play itself matters more than the place. Unhurried.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭にツバメの巣ができて喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were so happy when the swallows built their nest in the garden, weren't you?
lines.style: Delighted recognition. Lighter than before — almost singing the memory. She's seen into something tender he might not say himself. Warm smile underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは炭水化物中心の食生活でらしたぞ
lines.en: Your father lived on rice and noodles when I was young, you know.
lines.style: Quiet observation, neither judgment nor complaint. Factual, almost bemused. Slight patience in the pacing — the way you speak of someone who's no longer here.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年はクールビズの服装でリラックスしてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And in his later years he was so comfortable in those light Cool Biz outfits, wasn't he?
lines.style: Tender recollection with a hint of gentle teasing. She's noticed something small and human about him — the contentment in comfort. Voice settles warmly.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと高島屋で買い物をしたぞ
lines.en: When I was young, your father and I went shopping together at Takashimaya.
lines.style: Quieter now, more introspective. The specificity of the place matters. Slow, deliberate delivery. Trailing slightly at the end — the memory is both vivid and very far away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、京都で芸者さんを見て驚かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You were so surprised when you saw the geishas in Kyoto, weren't you?
lines.style: Bright, knowing completion. She's tying threads together. Warm and slightly mischievous — she loves that she knows these pieces of him. Voice lands gently, like closing a chapter.
